study type: Prospective cohort study and cross-sectional study
exposure: Body site (stool, oral gingiva, nares, skin, vagina)
Time point (at delivery vs. 6 weeks after delivery)
outcome: Taxonomic composition of the neonatal and early infant microbiota
Metabolic function of the neonatal and early infant microbiota
cohort: 81 pregnant women and their infants, with longitudinal sampling through 6 weeks after delivery, and a second matched cross-sectional cohort (n=81) sampled at delivery
finding: While the neonatal microbiota was relatively homogeneous across body sites at birth, it diversified by 6 weeks of age, primarily driven by body site and not mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Although minor variations in the neonatal microbiota were associated with cesarean delivery in some body sites at birth, this was not observed in stool, and there were no differences in community structure or function between delivery modes at 6 weeks.
